rule: Each of the 26 published grammar items (data/gold_morphology.json) against the blind answer runs/answers/K2_morph.json, read in real spelling (src/unscramble.py; its morphemes, word classes and formulas). right: the answer's main reading is the published function; partly: the item is found but its function is named only in part, or given to a neighbouring segment; missed: not found. The run recognised Meroitic (it says so), so this measures memory as much as inference.

items.proposed: -l: Determiner, singular (a definite article 'the').
-leb: Plural determiner ('the' + plural).

items.published: plural marker inside the determiner and pronouns
items.proposed: -b-: Plural marker, found inside longer endings.
-s: Genitive or relational postposition 'of'.

items.published: synthetic genitive: possessor + determiner + head noun
items.proposed: -li: Determiner in its linking (non-final) form ... (a possessor before a kin noun).
-te: Locative or origin 'in, at, from (a place)'.

items.published: directional locative in 'from X to Y'
local postposition in 'from X to Y'

items.proposed: -i: Vocative (address) on the invoked divine names.
-lowi built from article + -o (predicative) + -wi (copula); -lo: 'is the', a short copula.
-lowi: Copula with determiner, singular: 'is (the) ...'; built from article + predicative + copula.

items.published: emphatic marker after the singular copula
items.proposed: -wi: Copula 'is' (predicative or assertive).
-lebkwi: Plural copula with determiner: 'they are (the) ...'.
qo: Demonstrative 'this'. It serves as the nominator ('this is NAME').

items.published: verbal dative 'to him/her', inside the verb
items.proposed: 'to him/her' put on the final ending -kes; Xe read as the verb root.
-bxes: Plural counterpart ...: plural beneficiaries ('to them').

items.published: plural imperative/optative ending, addressed to Isis and Osiris
items.proposed: -kes (-ke te / -kete): Final person and number ending: singular beneficiary ('to him/her'), with the two invoked gods as subject ('may you give').

items.published: verbal prefix of benediction verbs, possibly optative
items.proposed: p- (pi-): Verbal prefix of the benediction verbs: optative or jussive mood ('may ...').

items.published: p- + s-element; the s-element's function unknown
items.proposed: Si / So / S: Constant verbal element after the prefix, probably the verb itself ('give').
tedxe: Parent slot 1, probably 'born of' (the mother).
terike: Parent slot 2, probably 'begotten by' (the father).
yetmde: The general relation term ...: 'relative of'.
